title: The Thing You Already Know
description: Homepage / paid / first-touch VSL. The prospect recognizes their own situation in 20 seconds, and by the end wants the loop running on their own customers.
oneIdea: You already had the answer. It was in a conversation nobody could search.
tone: confident, quiet, a little haunting at the open. No hype, no stock-photo optimism, no AI-powered.

cta.label: Upload a conversation
cta.supporting: Bring one conversation. See what it already knows.

scenes.name: Act I — The Cold Open
scenes.picture: Black. White text, one line at a time, unhurried. Then a waveform scrubbing past; it stops; a transcript line surfaces. No logo.

beats.onScreen: In March, a customer told you exactly why they'd leave.

beats.voiceover: They told you. On a call. Somewhere around minute nineteen.
beats.caption: They told you. On a call. Minute nineteen.

beats.voiceover: Nobody wrote it down. Nobody could have found it if they had.
beats.onScreen: Honestly? Onboarding took three weeks and I never got the hours back.
beats.caption: Nobody wrote it down. Nobody could have found it.

beats.onScreen: You didn't miss the signal. You had it.

scenes.name: Act II — The Real Problem
scenes.picture: Wall of artifacts sliding past: call recordings, Notion doc, survey rows, laptop notes, Slack thread. Collapses into a grey folder, dragged onto a stack of identical folders.

beats.voiceover: You do talk to customers. That was never the problem.
beats.caption: You do talk to customers. That was never the problem.

beats.voiceover: The problem is that every conversation starts from zero — and ends in a place nobody will ever look again.
beats.caption: Every conversation starts from zero.
Research goes in. Nothing compounds.

beats.voiceover: So you learn the same thing four times, from four customers, in four quarters. And you act on none of it, because "I think I heard that somewhere" doesn't survive a leadership meeting.
beats.caption: You learn the same thing four times. And act on none of it.

scenes.name: Act III — The Turn
scenes.picture: Cut to white. First product frame: a single quote card with a name, a date, and a play button. Multiplies into a constellation. Logo lands as relief.

beats.voiceover: What if every conversation made the next one sharper?
beats.caption: What if every conversation made the next one sharper?

beats.voiceover: Not a summary. Not a vibe. Evidence you can play back.
beats.caption: Not a summary. Not a vibe. Evidence you can play back.

scenes.name: Beat 1 — The interview
scenes.picture: Phone on a kitchen counter. Interview in progress, no interviewer. Uppy's next question changes. Split three ways: typed, spoken, video. Citation: Lucas et al., 2014.

beats.voiceover: You can't interview four hundred customers. So Uppy does.
beats.caption: You can't interview four hundred customers. So Uppy does.

beats.voiceover: Not a form. An actual conversation — it hears what they said and asks the better next question.
beats.caption: Not a form. An actual conversation.

beats.voiceover: And they answer however they want. Typed. Spoken. On camera.
beats.caption: Typed. Spoken. On camera.

beats.voiceover: Which means you don't just get the words. You get the sigh before them.
beats.caption: You don't just get the words. You get the sigh before them.

beats.voiceover: And here's the strange part. People tell a machine things they won't tell you.
beats.onScreen: People disclose more when they believe no human is listening. Lucas et al., 2014
beats.caption: People tell a machine things they won't tell you.

beats.voiceover: No performance. No managing your feelings. Just what they actually think.
beats.onScreen: People disclose more when they believe no human is listening. Lucas et al., 2014
beats.caption: No performance. Just what they actually think.

scenes.name: Beat 1b — The profile thickens
scenes.picture: Dana's card grows: call, survey, video. Then Uppy skips two questions — already answered, June.

beats.voiceover: The first conversation tells you a little.
beats.caption: The first conversation tells you a little.

beats.voiceover: The fifth tells you who she is. What she's trying to do. What almost made her leave. Every single thing with a receipt you can play.
beats.caption: The fifth tells you who she is. With a receipt you can play.

beats.voiceover: So it never asks her the same question twice. It starts where you left off.
beats.caption: It never asks the same question twice.

scenes.name: Beat 2 — The pattern
scenes.picture: Nine quotes snap into a cluster: Onboarding takes too long. Count: 14 people. Click opens faces and sentences. One clip plays.

beats.voiceover: When fourteen customers circle the same thing, you don't get a hunch. You get fourteen names and fourteen clips.
beats.caption: Fourteen names. Fourteen clips.

beats.voiceover: This is what makes it undeniable in a room.
beats.caption: This is what makes it undeniable in a room.

scenes.name: Beat 3 — Who thinks it
scenes.picture: Theme splits into Founders vs Enterprise buyers. Then a group tile: Churn risk — 9 people. A tenth face slides in.

beats.voiceover: And it splits by who they are. Because what your founders want and what your enterprise buyers want are not the same product decision.
beats.caption: What founders want and what enterprise buyers want are not the same decision.

beats.voiceover: Groups keep themselves current. Somebody says the wrong thing on a Tuesday, and they're in the group before you've read the transcript.
beats.caption: Somebody says the wrong thing on a Tuesday. They're in the group.

scenes.name: Beat 4 — The question
scenes.picture: From the group, an outreach draft writes itself. Questions appear with because-she-said-this receipts. Two greyed out. Then: would you be open to fifteen minutes?

beats.voiceover: Then it goes back out. To exactly those nine people.
beats.onScreen: You mentioned onboarding took three weeks…
beats.caption: Then it goes back out. To exactly those nine people.

beats.voiceover: It asks what you still don't know — built from what they already told you. Nothing generic. Nothing twice.
beats.caption: Nothing generic. Nothing twice.

beats.voiceover: And because you told it what this conversation is for, it asks for the thing you actually wanted.
beats.onScreen: …and would you be open to fifteen minutes?
beats.caption: It asks for the thing you actually wanted.

scenes.name: Beat 5 — Waiting on
scenes.picture: Waiting on list. Dana said yes Tuesday, books a slot, row turns green and leaves. Quote joins the cluster. Count 14 → 15. Profile gains a line.

beats.voiceover: Every one of these is a loop somebody opened and nobody closed.
beats.caption: A loop somebody opened and nobody closed.

beats.voiceover: It follows up. It notices when they book. It closes itself.
beats.caption: It follows up. It notices when they book. It closes itself.

beats.voiceover: And the whole thing gets smarter for the next person.
beats.caption: And the whole thing gets smarter for the next person.

scenes.name: Act V — The Proof
scenes.picture: Clean type, one line at a time, each with a small artifact. Churn → ICP → roadmap.

beats.voiceover: The churn reason, in their words, before the renewal call.
beats.onScreen: Know why they leave — while they're still here.
beats.caption: The churn reason, in their words, before the renewal call.

beats.voiceover: Stop guessing who your best customer is. Watch which one keeps telling you the same thing.
beats.onScreen: Sell to the segment that actually buys.
beats.caption: Stop guessing who your best customer is.

beats.voiceover: With fourteen clips behind it, the roadmap argument is over in ninety seconds.
beats.caption: Fourteen clips. The roadmap argument is over.

scenes.name: Act VI — Close
scenes.picture: Back to black. March quote now sits inside a cluster, in a group, with a follow-up already sent and answered. Cursor on Upload a conversation.

beats.voiceover: You already had the answer.
beats.onScreen: Honestly? Onboarding took three weeks and I never got the hours back.
beats.caption: You already had the answer.

beats.voiceover: Now you'll be able to find it.
beats.caption: Now you'll be able to find it.
